the synthetic pyrethroid and organophosphorus insecticides are equally effective in controlling the bollworms complex of cotton, but the synthetic pyrethrins are comparatively more expensive.

the alternate spray of monocrotophors 36 WSC or cypermerthrn 10EC, or fenvalerate 10EC or endosulfan, 35EC at an interval of about 15 - 18 days is most effective and economically sound to control the bolls of cotton.

the spray schedule consisting of alternate sprays of cypermethrin 10 EC + monocrotophos (36 WSC) + endosulfan (35 EC) + fenvalerate (20 EC) at an interval of about 15 - 25 days, proved to be the most effective schedule for the control of the bollworms of cotton.

alternate sprays of synthetic pyrethoids and organophosphates are more effective in controlling cotton bollworm complex than the single sprays and also more economical.

alternate spraying of monocrotophose 36 WSC and cypermethrin 10 EC at an interval 15 to 20 days is most effective and economical schedule for the control of bollworms complex of cotton in the field conditions.
